question: What is the primary risk associated with the reuse of needles and syringes?
explanation: Unsafe injection practices directly transmit infectious agents like hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV through contaminated equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why do patients frequently remain silent about injection safety during routine care?

options.A: Patients universally understand sterile technique principles
options.B: Implicit trust and systemic barriers prevent active questioning
options.C: Oral medications are always preferred over parenteral routes
options.D: Hospital policies mandate that patients inspect all medical supplies

explanation: Power imbalances and lack of health literacy stop patients from scrutinizing clinical procedures performed by professionals. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: How does hierarchical healthcare structures typically affect patient questioning?

options.A: It encourages rigorous inspection of medical equipment
options.B: It promotes equal collaborative treatment planning
options.C: It suppresses patients from voicing safety concerns
options.D: It eliminates all forms of health illiteracy

explanation: Steep power gradients make patients hesitant to challenge authority figures regarding their clinical practices. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient notices a nurse picking up a syringe from an open tray but stays quiet because the doctor ordered the shot. This silence is best explained by which concept?
explanation: Patients defer to perceived expertise, assuming professionals know best and making them reluctant to speak up. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary consequence of low health literacy regarding injections?

options.A: Higher rates of oral medication compliance
options.B: Inability to recognize hazardous infection control practices
options.C: Better understanding of multi-dose vial risks
options.D: Increased insistence on sterile single-use packaging

explanation: Without basic knowledge of transmission routes, patients cannot identify when a healthcare provider violates safety standards. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which factor best describes why a patient accepts an injection without verifying if the needle is new?

options.A: Ignorance of the risks associated with contaminated equipment
options.B: Advanced understanding of hospital sterilization protocols
options.C: Explicit desire to contract a bloodborne viral infection
options.D: Absolute rejection of professional medical advice

explanation: Patients accept unsafe practices simply because they do not know that equipment reuse spreads serious infections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why do many cultural groups strongly prefer injections over oral medications?

options.A: Pills are significantly more expensive to manufacture
options.B: Injections are perceived to work faster and more potently
options.C: Oral medications require specialized medical training
options.D: Injections completely eliminate all side effects

explanation: A widespread cultural belief holds that piercing the skin delivers medicine directly to the ailment for a quicker cure. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: How does a strong cultural desire for parenteral therapy impact patient vigilance?

options.A: It promotes detailed questioning about medication ingredients
options.B: It encourages strict auditing of hospital waste disposal bins
options.C: It eliminates the power imbalance in the clinic room
options.D: It distracts the patient from observing whether sterile techniques are used

explanation: When patients are preoccupied with obtaining their preferred treatment, they overlook safety checks entirely. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: What stops some patients from reporting unsafe clinical practices to staff?

options.A: Belief that staff appreciate constructive criticism
options.B: Confidence that the facility conducts internal audits
options.D: Fear of retaliation and compromised future care

explanation: Vulnerable patients worry that challenging staff will result in mistreatment or refusal of vital medical services. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: A patient notices a dirty treatment surface but says nothing, worrying the nurse will refuse to treat them next time. This scenario highlights which barrier?

options.A: Superior health literacy regarding infection risks
options.B: Systemic intimidation and dependency on the provider
options.C: Clear understanding of institutional reporting channels
options.D: Cultural preference for rapid pharmacological action

explanation: Dependency on healthcare access creates an environment of intimidation where patients choose silence to protect their care. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which institutional factor directly contributes to rushed procedures and missed safety steps?

options.B: Abundant supplies of sterile disposable equipment
options.C: Severe staff shortages and heavy workloads
options.D: Rigorous routine safety audits by management

explanation: Overworked healthcare personnel juggling high patient volumes often cut corners, normalizing unsafe shortcuts. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is meant by the term 'normalization of deviance' in healthcare settings?

options.A: Staff members openly report all minor clinical errors
options.B: Unsafe shortcuts gradually become accepted as standard practice
options.C: Hospitals strictly enforce international sterilization guidelines
options.D: Patients routinely demand single-use packaging for every drug

explanation: When dangerous breaches happen repeatedly without immediate disaster, staff and patients alike begin accepting them as normal. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: How can nurses help overcome patient passivity regarding injection safety?

options.A: By discouraging patients from looking at medical supplies
options.B: By ignoring patient concerns to save valuable time
options.C: By actively encouraging questions and educating the community
options.D: By enforcing strict hierarchy within the clinic room

explanation: Nurses empower patients through open communication, demystifying procedures and welcoming safety inquiries. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)

question: A nurse takes time to show a patient the unbroken seal on a new syringe before administration. Which professional goal does this action achieve?

options.A: Proving the superiority of oral medications over injections
options.B: Building trust and reducing patient anxiety about safety
options.C: Demonstrating compliance with institutional rationing policies
options.D: Complying with punitive measures from hospital administration

explanation: Transparently demonstrating safety measures reassures the patient and fosters a collaborative therapeutic relationship. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)
